title.narrative: Output 5.2. Increased capacity of Member States to strengthen skills and lifelong learning policies, governance models and financing system

description.narrative: In February 2023, a new education and Training policy 2023 was endorsed and adopted by the Ministry of Education. Prior to the endorsement, the policy was reviewed and validated by social partners and other national stakeholders. The policy includes provisions on skills anticipation and matching, recognition of prior learning and green TVET. The policy document also adopted inclusive provisions responding to the needs and interests of migrants, PWD, women and refugees. In July 2022 the ILO constituents participated in study mission to India and got exposure on sector skills council governance and institutional arrangement. This was followed by a technical and policy dialogue on establishing sectors skills councils and quality apprenticeship programmes in Pretoria in July 2023. As a result, a national road map that will guide national dialogue and consultations on establishing inclusive skills governance and quality apprenticeships is developed. The study visits and Policy dialogue is part of the capacity building of national constituents through South- South Cooperation programme of the ILO. With the support from the Norwegian development cooperation Agency and the United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, the ILO supported national consultative workshops in March and April 2022 during the development and review of the Education and training policy. The ILO also provided technical inputs into the draft policy document. In addition, the ILO provided technical guidance to the drafting team using ILO tools on skills policy formulation guided by the policy brief on Formulating national Policy on Skills development. The ILO through the SSTC programme supported and a facilitated the study mission to India and participation of the Ethiopian officials to a high-level policy dialogue on quality apprenticeship in Pretoria. In addition, the ILO provided technical presentation during which ILO’s toolkits for quality apprenticeships w Volume 1 and Volume 2 were used as guiding documents for policy and practitioners.

description.narrative: In March 2023, 41 (18 men and 23 women) tourism and hospitality graduate students trained on core skills which promote school to work transition. In June 2022, the Ministry of Labour and Skills validated and endorsed the Basic English for Workplace Communication training manual targeting potential migrants. The training manual, inclusive of trainers and trainee’s handbook, is developed to improve English language for potential migrant workers' quicker integration into and improved access to the labour markets of destination countries. In 2023, capacity of (8) Technical and vocational training institutions in Ethiopia to deliver quality training was strengthened through equipment and tools support. As result 5,254 (56 young men, 5198 young women) now have access to quality training from these centres due to improve capacity. The support target selected TVET centres training potential and returned migrants in hotel and tourism, hairdressing, domestic work, and bakery sector. In June 2022, Jijiga Polytechnic developed and adopted flexible short term TVET courses to address skills gaps among the refugees and host community youth in priority occupations aligned to economic opportunities in Somalia regional state of Ethiopia. As a result, 170 trainees enrolled; out of which 95 of them are people with disability from refugees, host and IDP communities. 55 of the graduates successfully completed and were certified. Ethiopian Poultry producers and Processors association (EPPA) to develop short courses on Poultry keeping and management that is delivered on the Job. The training modules were adopted by key stakeholders. 200 graduates interested in poultry sector are registered to enrol in the programme. In addition, 15 poultry farm supervisors have received ToT to facilitate delivery of this course to interested trainees at the Poultry farms. On core work skills, the ILO supported and facilitated the trainings on core work skill by using ILO’s core skills framework developed for Ethiopia. The ILO developed and delivered the training. the with the support of the United Kingdom Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office, ILO provided technical support and facilitated Drafting, review, and validation workshops for the Ministry of Labour and Skills in revising and redesigning the existing Basic Language Communication Skills Module for workplace communication of the Government of Ethiopia to better respond to the needs of potential migrants. The ILO also supported and facilitated ToT to TVET trainers on the new English training Language manual. In Addition, the, ILO facilitated the assessment of the capacity of technical and vocational training Centres in Ethiopia to provide quality training to potential and returned migrants. Based on the findings and recommendations the ILO equipped their workshops with up-to-date learning tools, equipment and machinery for quality, practical and friendly learning environment. This led to the provision of quality training to 5254 beneficiaries in selected sector The ILO reviewed and provided technical guidance on the design and delivery of the short courses by utilizing ILO tools such as Making TVET and skills systems inclusive of people with disability Policy brief.

Output 5.1. Increased capacity of Member States to identify current skills mismatches and anticipate future skill needs

description.narrative: In response to the growing need for high skilled workers at managerial, supervisory and policy making level in the tourism sector, the Addis Ababa University developed a PhD programme in Tourism management and Development. The University is launching the Tourism management and development course in September 2023. The course is aligned to the aspiration of Home-grown economic reform agenda as well as based on the ILO core skills framework. Similarly, in May 2023 green TVT assessment report was launched identifying amongst others green skills needs at the TVT level. The report was validated at a tripartite workshop. The report provides actionable recommendations towards promoting green skills in the TVT sector. The report was developed in collaboration with the Ministry of Labour and Skills, TVT colleges, regional labour and skills and other partners. Green TVT is one of the key thematic areas in the new Education and Training policy 2023. The ILO provided technical inputs by reviewing the draft documents such as ToRs, Draft reports on needs assessment for PhD programme; the ILO also provided financial resources that facilitated the whole process. In addition, the ILO supported and implemented a training to 138 participants (of which 52 are women and 86 are men) on skills for greener future for tourism and hospitality sector, and environmental sustainability for women led SMEs. The training aims at building the capacity of key partners in utilizing green concepts and methodologies in their sectors or areas of work. In April 2023, green TVET training conducted using the ILO’s Greening TVET and skills Development: Practical guidance tool . 47 TVT instructors, university teachers and other partners participated.
